groups.title: MVC Architecture and Rails Philosophy
groups.question: You are starting a Rails app for a recipe site. Explain how Rails organises the code and why you rarely write configuration.

followUps.Model-View-Controller pattern in Rails: What does each part of MVC do in a Rails request?
followUps.Convention over configuration Rails prin: What does convention over configuration mean in practice?
followUps.Rails project directory structure overvi: Where would you find models, routes and configuration in a Rails app?

evidence.text: Models handle data and business rules.
Controllers handle the request and decide what to do.
Views render the response, usually HTML.

notEnough: Only spelling out Model, View, Controller.

evidence.text: Rails assumes sensible defaults.
Naming conventions connect classes, files and tables automatically, such as a Recipe model and a recipes table.
This removes most setup code, as long as you follow the conventions.
app holds models, views, controllers and other application code.
config holds routes and settings.
db holds migrations and the schema.

groups.title: Routing and Request Handling
groups.question: You need pages to list, create, edit and delete recipes, and you want a working version quickly. Explain how routing and generators help.

followUps.Routes, controllers, and resourceful rou: What does resources :recipes create in the routes?
followUps.Rails generators and scaffolding workflo: What do generators and scaffolding give you, and what are their limits?

evidence.text: Routes map HTTP methods and URLs to controller actions.
resources generates the seven standard actions for a resource in one line.
This follows REST conventions, such as GET for index and DELETE for destroy.
Generators create models, controllers, views and migrations.
Scaffolding builds a full working CRUD interface for a resource.
Scaffold code is a starting point that usually needs editing for real use.

groups.title: Rails Development Tools
groups.question: A page shows the wrong recipes and you are not sure what SQL ran. Explain how you would explore the app and trace the request.

followUps.Rails console for live app exploration: How does the Rails console help you explore the app?
followUps.Development server and request logging: What does the development log show for each request?

evidence.text: The console opens Ruby with the whole app loaded.
You can query the database and call model methods directly.
It is quick for checking data and testing code.

notEnough: Only saying it is a shell.

evidence.text: rails server starts the local web server.
Each request is logged with its controller action and parameters.
The log shows the SQL queries and how long each part took.

groups.title: Views and Template Rendering
groups.question: Every page needs the same header, and after saving a recipe the user should see 'Recipe saved'. Explain how layouts and flash messages work.

followUps.ERB templates and layout inheritance: How does a layout wrap each view?
followUps.Flash messages and redirect patterns: Why use a redirect with a flash message after saving a form?

evidence.text: ERB embeds Ruby in HTML templates.
The layout holds the shared page structure.
yield in the layout marks where each action's view is inserted.
Flash stores a short message for the next request only.
Redirecting after a successful save prevents a duplicate submit on refresh.
The layout shows the flash message on the page the user lands on.
